# Prompt Gallery Full-Stack TanStack rebuild task

Agent: codex-main
Source HTML: makeup.html

Convert makeup.html into a production full-stack TanStack Start product in this directory.

Requirements:
- Use a real TanStack Start application structure, including the appropriate app/vite/start configuration and file based routing under src/routes. Do not make a plain Vite-only React app with a decorative TanStack dependency.
- Preserve the original page's visual identity, typography, responsive layout, and interactions from makeup.html.
- Recreate the complete frontend product experience from the source page: the POWERPROMPT brand, sticky sidebar/navigation, top model filter bar, sort controls, search reveal, masonry-style prompt gallery, varied media card aspect ratios, image-based prompt previews, hover overlays, save/favorite behavior, cart/dock actions, toast feedback, lightbox/detail preview, and mobile drawer/dock layout.
- Keep the source domain vocabulary visible where it belongs, including the original model/filter/sort concepts such as GPT-4o, Claude, Midjourney, Flux, Featured, Newest, Popular, Favorites, and Cart.
- Split meaningful UI into React components instead of leaving one giant HTML string.
- Keep styles maintainable in source files that belong to the app.
- Add a real backend layer for the prompt marketplace. Use TanStack Start server functions, API routes, or server-side route loaders/actions for catalog reads, search/filtering, favorites/cart mutations, checkout simulation, and creator/admin analytics.
- Add a local database layer with seed data derived from the source page. SQLite is preferred. Keep schema, seed data, and query helpers in source-controlled files. If you choose a file database, it must be created under the project workspace only.
- Implement database-side calculations, not just frontend array math. Required computed data includes prompt ranking, featured/free filters, cart totals, creator revenue, conversion rate, average price, category totals, and daily sales or trend summaries.
- Surface those backend/database values in the UI through routes, loaders, API calls, or server functions. Include at least a storefront route, prompt detail route, cart or checkout route, and creator/admin analytics route.
- Provide npm scripts for dev, build, and start or preview.
- Provide more than one test command. Include unit tests for database/query calculations, API/server-function tests for backend behavior, and a browser/component/e2e smoke test for the main user flows.
- Install Playwright by default in package.json, preferably both @playwright/test and playwright or whichever your browser test imports.
- Install any required dependencies in package.json.
- Verify with npm install, npm run build, the database/API/unit test scripts, and at least one browser smoke check.
- Do not ask the user questions or stop early while the task can still be completed locally. Keep setting up the environment, fixing failures, running the required tests, and iterating until the app is complete and the tests pass. Only ask a question if the current environment truly cannot run the required validation after reasonable setup effort.
- Do not read or compare against the sibling makeup-codex or makeup-tura project.

item.text: I’ve got the brief and the source. The original is a polished single-page POWERPROMPT gallery with the exact interaction set we need; I’m going to keep its visual DNA but move state, filtering, checkout, and analytics behind a real app/data boundary.

item.text: The environment has Node 22 and current TanStack packages available. I’m choosing a compact stack: TanStack Start routes, server functions, a local JSON-backed database module with query helpers that centralize the marketplace calculations, and API route tests around that boundary.

I’m about to lay down the project files: package/config first, then the database and route/component code. The data layer will seed from the original LOTS array and use SQL queries for ranking, totals, conversion, revenue, and trends so the browser isn’t doing the marketplace math.
Config is in place. Next I’m adding the seeded local database, with the original prompt vocabulary expanded into creators, categories, orders, favorites, and cart rows.

A quick note on the database choice: I’m using `sql.js`, which gives us a real local SQLite database file without native compilation friction on Windows. The app still executes SQL for the required business calculations and persists the seeded DB under this workspace.

The SQLite layer is now seeded and queryable. I’m moving on to the app shell and routes: storefront, detail, cart/checkout, and creator analytics, with the original left rail, sticky filter bar, gallery hover behavior, dock, toast, and mobile drawer mapped into React components.

item.text: I’m adding the server-function layer now. This keeps client interactions simple, but mutations like save, cart, and checkout still cross a backend boundary and update the local database.

The Start entry points and root loader are in. I’m shaping the UI into reusable components now, keeping the original composition: sidebar, sticky filters, masonry cards, lightbox/detail preview, dock, toast, and mobile drawer.

The shell is wired. I’m adding the storefront route next: filter/search state lives in the URL, the list comes from the server loader, and card actions call server functions with a toast and route refresh.

I noticed the app shell belongs at the root rather than as its own page route, so I’m folding it into the root document and keeping the storefront as `src/routes/index.tsx`. That gives all pages the same sidebar/dock frame.

Storefront route is in place with URL-driven model, category, search, sort, Favorites, and free filters. I’m adding the product detail, cart/checkout, and analytics pages now so the marketplace flow is complete.
The core pages are in. I’m applying the styling now, adapted from the source page but organized for the React app and expanded for cart/admin screens and mobile behavior.
The visual layer is mostly done. I’m adding focused tests now: database calculations, server-function behavior, and Playwright smoke coverage for gallery, detail, cart, and mobile drawer.

Tests are written. I’m going back to dependency installation now; the first attempt left a partial `node_modules`, so I’ll retry normally first and only remove the local partial install if npm still can’t repair itself.

item.text:
Implemented the POWERPROMPT TanStack Start marketplace end to end.

What changed:
- Built a real TanStack Start app with file routes under `src/routes`.
- Recreated the source experience: sidebar, sticky filters, search reveal, sort/model vocabulary, masonry gallery, varied image cards, hover overlays, favorites, cart dock, toast feedback, detail preview, mobile drawer/dock.
- Added local SQLite via `sql.js`, seeded at `data/powerprompt.sqlite`.
- Added backend/server-function boundary in `src/market-api.ts`.
- Added storefront, prompt detail, cart/checkout simulation, and creator analytics routes.
- Added database/API/e2e test suites.
- Added production built server wrapper so `npm run start` serves the SSR app reliably from `dist`.

Verified:
- `npm install`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:db`
- `npm run test:api`
- `npm run test:e2e`

All passed. One note: `npm install` reports existing dependency audit findings from installed packages, but the requested build and tests are green. I also could not run `git status` because Git flagged `C:/` as a dubious ownership repository root in this environment.
